title: Nawabs of Bengal
capsule: The Nawabs of Bengal held autonomous power over the richest province of the Mughal Empire from 1717, when Murshid Quli Khan was recognized by Emperor Farrukhsiyar as hereditary Nawab Nazim, effectively governing Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa from Murshidabad. Under Alivardi Khan (r. 1740–1756) the nawabate repelled sixteen years of Maratha incursions while maintaining fiscal independence from Delhi. The Battle of Plassey (23 June 1757), in which Robert Clive's East India Company forces defeated Siraj ud-Daulah after the defection of Mir Jafar, ended effective nawabi sovereignty; subsequent battles at Buxar (1764) confirmed Company supremacy. Thereafter the title survived as a ceremonial dignity under Company-imposed puppets until its administrative significance was extinguished.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The nawabate's territorial extent — Bengal proper, Bihar, and Orissa — is well documented from Mughal administrative records and East India Company correspondence; the to date of 1762 in this dataset reflects the loss of effective sovereignty rather than the formal end of the title.
